name: replaceme-platform-rules
description: Platform rules on main. Generated games (world.json on game/<slug> branches) may only use the controls, mechanics and scoring spec defined here. Humans and the actor use the SAME controls; the actor never invents values outside these actions. See shared/game_contract.md.

interact.input: Enter or E, or click on an NPC/station/submit target

control_semantics.point_or_target: either {"target_id": string} or {"x": number, "y": number}; x,y are in observation.viewport coordinates
control_semantics.key_press: a key action with hold_ms=0 is one press = one step. hold_ms>0 repeats: steps = 1 + floor(hold_ms / 100). Human keyboard auto-repeat produces the same per-keydown steps
control_semantics.world_walk: when no level is open, key_* moves the avatar one tile per step (blocked by map.solids); interact next to an NPC/location opens its quest or level
control_semantics.virtual_time: in agent mode (?agent=1) game time advances ONLY through actions: key press 100 ms, key hold hold_ms, mouse_click 50 ms, mouse_drag duration_ms, wait ms, others 0 ms. Same action sequence -> same observations and score. Human mode uses real time
control_semantics.score_card: when a level ends (pass or fail) a score card shows score 0-100, passed, qualitative feedback and per-term breakdown labels (never targets). interact or any click dismisses it; no extra buttons

observation.description: Structured state returned by window.__replaceme.observe() and act(). NEVER contains scoring targets, tolerances, correct answers or points.

fields.mechanic: mix | timing | sort | deliver | converse | null
fields.t_ms: number, game time since level start
fields.aim: string, what to achieve (not the answer)
fields.controls_hint: string, e.g. 'Up/Down choose, Left/Right adjust, Enter to brew'
fields.viewport: { w, h } coordinate space for every x,y
fields.avatar: { x, y, tile: [col,row], facing, carrying: string | null }
fields.grid: { cols, rows, blocked: [[col,row], ...] } walkable grid (world phase and deliver)
fields.targets: [{ id, kind: slider|button|npc|location|item|bin|choice|meter|spot|submit, label, x, y, w, h, enabled }] every clickable/interactable thing with its position
fields.focus: string | null, target id of the current keyboard selection
fields.messages: [{ speaker, npc_id, text, t_ms }] recent dialogue and hints
fields.last_result: null | { score, passed, feedback: [string], breakdown: { term_id: { label, score } } }

mix.title: Mix / set amounts
mix.description: Set the amount or setting of each ingredient or process variable, then brew/stir/submit. Covers cooking, potion making, brewing, dosing, configuring.
mix.input_mapping: key_up/key_down select variable; key_left/key_right change selected value by -/+ step per press step; mouse_drag slider:<var_id> handle or mouse_click on slider:<var_id> track sets value at that position (snapped to step); mouse_click ingredient:<id> appends to add order (only if params.ingredients); interact or mouse_click submit scores

params.station_id: string, map location the level opens at
params.variables: [{ id, label, unit, min, max, step, default }] (1-6)

mix.observation: { variables: [{ id, label, unit, min, max, step, value }], selected_index, added_order: [ingredient_id] }
mix.aim: Produce the best result by choosing the right values.
mix.scoring: numeric spec: scoring.variables + scoring.derived (+ optional scoring.order)
fail_conditions: time_limit_ms elapsed before submit (score computed on current values)

timing.title: Timing / hold and release
timing.description: Stop a moving meter, or hold and release, inside the right zone. Covers steaming, pouring, kneading, heating, waiting for doneness.
timing.input_mapping: phase.mode 'stop': the needle sweeps min->max->min with period_ms (triangle wave from min at phase start); interact, key_up or mouse_click meter stops it. phase.mode 'hold': value = min + fill_per_s * held_seconds (clamped to max); hold with mouse_down meter ... mouse_up, or key_up with hold_ms. Each phase ends when stopped/released; next phase starts

params.phases: [{ id, label, unit, min, max, mode: stop|hold, period_ms?, fill_per_s? }] (1-3)

timing.observation: { phase_index, phases_total, meter: { id, label, unit, min, max, value, moving, holding }, results: [{ id, value }] }
timing.aim: Stop or release at the right moment for each phase.
timing.scoring: numeric spec: scoring.variables keyed by phase id (value = stopped/released value)

sort.title: Sort / route
sort.description: Route each item to the correct bin or slot. Covers bussing tables, filing papers, restocking, triage.
sort.input_mapping: items arrive one at a time in params order; key_left/key_right select bin; key_down or interact drops current item in the selected bin; mouse_drag item:<id> -> bin:<id>, or mouse_click bin:<id> drops the current item there

params.items: [{ id, label, icon?, attributes?: { key: string } }] (3-12, fixed order)

sort.observation: { current_item: { id, label, attributes } | null, queue_remaining, bins: [{ id, label }], selected_bin, placed: [{ item_id, bin_id }] }
sort.aim: Put every item where it belongs.
sort.scoring: scoring.correct { item_id: bin_id }, optional scoring.weights { item_id: w }, scoring.feedback { item_id: message when wrong }

deliver.title: Deliver / carry
deliver.description: Pick items up and carry them across the map to the right NPC, table or spot under time pressure. Covers serving, running food, couriering.
deliver.input_mapping: arrows walk the avatar one tile per step on the world map (observation.grid); interact (or mouse_click on an adjacent target) picks up at a pickup spot or hands over at a destination; capacity items carried at once

params.orders: [{ id, item, label, from: target_id, to: target_id }] (1-5)
params.par_ms: number, time for full time score

deliver.observation: { orders: [{ id, label, to_label, status: waiting|carrying|delivered|wrong }], carrying: [order_id] }
deliver.aim: Deliver every order to the right place quickly.
deliver.scoring: accuracy = sum(w correct deliveries)/sum(w); time_score = 1 if t <= par_ms, else linear to 0 at time_limit_ms; score = 100 * (weights.accuracy*accuracy + weights.time*time_score) / (weights.accuracy + weights.time). scoring.feedback { wrong_target, late, missed }

converse.title: Converse / transact
converse.description: Talk with an NPC and pick the right responses. Covers taking orders, settling a check, handling complaints, advising.
converse.input_mapping: each turn the NPC line appears (dialogue event); key_up/key_down select an option, interact confirms, or mouse_click choice:<option_id>; the NPC answers with the option's reply line

params.turns: [{ id, npc_line, options: [{ id, text, reply }] }] (2-6 turns, 2-4 options, linear order)

converse.observation: { npc: { id, name }, turn_index, turns_total, line, options: [{ id, text }], selected_index, history: [{ turn_id, option_id }] }
converse.scoring: scoring.turns { turn_id: { option_id: { points: 0..1, feedback, critical?: bool } } }; score = 100 * mean(points of chosen options)
fail_conditions: a critical option chosen (level ends, score = min(score, pass_threshold - 1))

scoring_spec.description: Declarative, deterministic scoring stored in world.json levels[].scoring. No randomness: same inputs -> same score. The game (TS) and any Python checker implement exactly these formulas.

fields.range: [lo, hi] optimal interval; deviation d = 0 inside, else distance to the nearest bound
fields.tolerance: number > 0, deviation at which quality is clearly degraded
fields.feedback: { too_low: string, too_high: string } qualitative, must not state the target

scoring_spec.variables: { var_id: numeric_term } for mix variables or timing phase ids
scoring_spec.derived: [{ id, label, expr, ...numeric_term }] expr uses only variable ids, numbers, + - * / ( ) and unary minus; division by zero -> s = 0
scoring_spec.order: optional (mix): { expected: [ingredient_id], weight, feedback: string } s = 1 if added_order equals expected else 0
scoring_spec.total: score = round(100 * sum(weight_i * s_i) / sum(weight_i), 1); passed = score >= pass_threshold
scoring_spec.feedback_rule: for each term with s < 0.8 emit feedback.too_low if value < target (or < range lo) else feedback.too_high; order by weight*(1-s) descending; at most 3 messages; if none, emit the level's success line
scoring_spec.expr_grammar: expr := term (('+'|'-') term)* ; term := factor (('*'|'/') factor)* ; factor := NUMBER | VAR_ID | '(' expr ')' | '-' factor ; VAR_ID := [a-z][a-z0-9_]*
